material.title: BIO unveils plan for US to remain biotech’s ‘global leader’
material.bodyOriginal: Two months after China unveiled a five-year plan to accelerate the ascent of its fast-rising biotechnology sector, a prominent lobbying group is pitching a policy proposal designed to help the U.S. maintain an edge in the field. The “action plan” by the Biotechnology Innovation Organization unveiled Tuesday lays out seven priorities Congress and the Trump administration should act on to “ensure” the U.S. remains the sector’s “global leader.” Called “BioAdvance: Securing America’s Biotech Century,” it involves ways to speed up drug development, improve the nation's clinical trial infrastructure, attract investment and better support biomedical research. BIO also calls on the U.S. to establish a “White House Office of Biotechnology” to help coordinate these plans and keep them on track. “This moment demands the ambition and determination that catalyzed the biotechnology revolution and made America the definitive global leader,” said BIO President and CEO John Crowley in a statement. BIO’s proposal comes amid an escalating debate among biotech executives, investors and lawmakers as to how to respond to China’s emergence as a drugmaking force. The U.S. has long been the world’s standard-bearer in developing new medicines. Yet China has made biotech progress a strategic priority and invested heavily in the sector over the last decade or so. That effort is now “paying off,” according to BIO. China now starts more than a quarter of the world’s clinical trials and initiates early-stage studies more quickly and cheaply. material.title: A single AI model simulates the behavior of many substances, from sliding sand to folding proteins
material.bodyOriginal: Today, a scientist who wants to simulate a physical process must pick the right tool for that one job, such as a solver built for flowing water or another designed to model the way a protein folds. Each one is hand-coded around the specific equations that dictate how that process behaves. Researchers at MIT, the University of British Columbia (UBC), and elsewhere have now replaced that patchwork with a single deep-learning system, called WorldParticle , that could help engineers model different physical phenomena, from sliding sand to folding proteins, with one unified artificial intelligence architecture. Scientists and engineers could use this system to model processes that typically require separate simulators, such as a fluid sloshing against a deformable solid. This could offer a faster, more accurate way to simulate how sloshing oil might impact an elastic valve in a storage tank, for instance. It could also help engineers study where and how granular materials, like sand or soil, could move when a soft robot touches them. The system represents every material it simulates, from a dune of sand to a protein molecule, as tiny particles and predicts where those particles will move one step at a time. Because it learns the underlying dynamics rather than being programmed with an equation, the model can adapt to materials, forces, and environments it never encountered during training. material.title: Martin Preyer
material.bodyOriginal: Martin Preyer, Dr. nat. techn. Martin Preyer is the director of biologics within the Center for the Development of Therapeutics (CDoT) at the Broad Institute of MIT and Harvard. He is building a biologics drug discovery organization to advance antibody-based programs alongside other Broad researchers. Preyer brings more than a decade of experience leading antibody-based drug discovery, from early target validation through IND-enabling studies. His primary areas of expertise include bispecific and multispecific antibody engineering, antibody-drug conjugates, and T cell engager platforms for oncology and immune-mediated disease. Before joining the Broad, Preyer was executive director of biotherapeutics at Evolveimmune Therapeutics, where he led a team advancing multiple programs toward IND-enabling studies and contributed to the IND filing for the company's lead program. Earlier, he built and led research organizations at Revitrope Oncology, Ohana Biosciences, and Flagship Labs 75. In these roles, he advanced novel biologics platforms from proof-of-concept through candidate selection, including a protease-activatable T-cell engager platform and a tissue-targeted multispecific/immunocytokine platform, and he is the inventor on multiple issued patents and pending applications covering bispecific and multispecific antibodies and platform technologies. Preyer holds a Dipl.-Ing. and a doctorate in biotechnology from BOKU University in Vienna, Austria. material.title: From patient communities to precision treatments: harnessing AI-powered biology for rare disease
material.bodyOriginal: Rare As One Network (Cycle 4) is Now Open for Applications Through December 15, 2026. Approximately 400 million people worldwide live with a rare disease. Of these diseases, fewer than 5% have an approved therapy. Many people with rare diseases carry not only the weight of a devastating diagnosis, but the isolation of navigating a biomedical research ecosystem that was not built with them in mind. We launched Rare As One in 2019 to catalyze a new path for these patients, investing in patient-led organizations to build research-ready communities, advance scientific understanding, and accelerate progress toward treatments and cures. This feels especially urgent today with the convergence of frontier AI and frontier biology redefining how biomedical scientists pursue the path from observation to treatment. AI-driven approaches are enabling researchers to interpret genetic variation, model disease mechanisms, and identify therapeutic opportunities with a speed and scale that would have seemed unimaginable only a few years ago. For rare diseases, many of which stem from a single genetic change with clear biological effects, the opportunity is especially profound. These conditions are among the most tractable for connecting genotype to phenotype, and often for translating that understanding into therapeutic opportunities. At Biohub, we are bringing together AI, biology, and patient communities to deepen understanding of disease biology and accelerate the development of precise and effective treatments. material.title: FDA Provides Clarity to Support Cell and Gene Therapy Development and Quality
material.bodyOriginal: FDA News Release FDA issues final guidance for cell and gene therapy manufacturers, recommends building potency assurance into every stage of a therapy’s lifecycle — from early development through patient delivery For Immediate Release: November 02, 2026 The U.S. Food and Drug Administration today issued final guidance for manufacturers of cellular and gene therapy (CGT) products to implement a comprehensive, science- and risk-based plan for making sure their products meet potency standards. The guidance provides FDA’s recommendations for a Potency Assurance Strategy, which guides manufacturers to test and verify — before a product reaches a patient — that every batch meets a defined standard of potency to do what the product is supposed to do therapeutically. The Potency Assurance for Cellular and Gene Therapy Products final guidance replaces FDA's 2011 potency testing guidance for CGT products and applies to treatments for serious and often life-threatening conditions. By law, manufacturers are expected to verify that their products work as intended, from the time of approval through post-approval monitoring. This final guidance provides FDA’s current thinking and recommendations on how manufacturers can meet that requirement. "Patients who receive cellular and gene therapies are often battling serious or life-threatening conditions, such as cancers and rare diseases, and they deserve the assurance that the product administered to them will perform as intended," said Karim Mikhail, B. material.title: How can we build trust in model-driven manufacturing?
material.bodyOriginal: Modern biopharma manufacturing faces many challenges, including process execution , observability , digital transformation and reliability . While each topic addresses a different aspect of manufacturing performance, they all contribute towards a common objective: creating greater confidence in how decisions are made. Over the last decade, biopharma manufacturers have invested heavily in automation, connectivity, data platforms and digital technologies while navigating the challenges of integrating legacy infrastructure and modern manufacturing systems to produce increasingly diverse therapeutic modalities. As a result, organizations today have access to more process, equipment and operational data than ever before. The challenge has moved from collecting information to using that information to anticipate outcomes before they occur. Historically, manufacturers have focused on understanding what happened. Increasingly, the goal is to understand what is likely to happen next. In many ways, this represents the next stage in the digital evolution of the industry, where confidence in predictive systems becomes just as important as the technology itself. Moving beyond hindsight toward model-driven bioprocess control For decades, manufacturing improvement has relied on hindsight: deviations occur, root causes are identified and corrective actions follow. While effective, this approach is labor-intensive, difficult to scale and increasingly challenged by demands for greater productivity, flexibility and efficiency. material.bodyOriginal: This audio is auto-generated. Please let us know if you have feedback . After a resounding victory in this week’s midterm elections, the Democratic Party has won control of both chambers of Congress. While the economy was the biggest issue in the election, plenty of candidates harped on the problem of healthcare costs as well. The topic is especially salient right now. Average employer-sponsored family coverage premiums rose 5% between 2025 and 2026, a KFF survey found. And employer healthcare costs are projected to rise 9.5% in 2027 before cost-mitigation measures, according to Aon . That added financial burden for Americans coincided with renewed interest in the “Medicare for all” idea in these midterms, especially among Democratic Congressional candidates. And because most roads in the healthcare cost debate eventually lead to drug prices, pharma also got attention from candidates on the campaign trail. While there’s bipartisan agreement on the goal of lowering drug prices, the parties diverge when it comes to how that should be accomplished. Under President Donald Trump, Republicans have become louder champions of most-favored nation pricing policies that link drug prices in America to what other countries pay. Democrats, on the other hand, are typically more in favor of price negotiations, such as the structure that was created for Medicare under the Inflation Reduction Act. material.bodyOriginal: The latest advances in cardiovascular medicine will take center stage at the American Heart Association (AHA) Scientific Sessions 2026 in Chicago from November 6 to 9. Bringing together researchers, clinicians, and industry leaders from around the world, the meeting will showcase new clinical findings and emerging approaches to tackling some of the biggest challenges in cardiovascular disease. This year’s program will highlight the growing diversity of strategies being explored, from RNA-based therapies and in vivo gene editing to new ways of targeting cardiovascular inflammation and the metabolic risk factors that drive heart disease. Several companies are also set to present clinical data that could offer new insights into the potential of these approaches, including treatments aimed at triglycerides, transthyretin amyloidosis, and cardiometabolic disease. However, the meeting comes against a backdrop of mixed results for the field, with recent setbacks in major cardiovascular trials underscoring just how difficult it is to translate promising biological targets into meaningful clinical benefits. In this article, we look at some of the key biotech developments, companies, and clinical data to watch at AHA Scientific Sessions 2026. material.title: Why one drug isn’t enough: AI reveals cancer’s secret weapon – and how to beat it
material.bodyOriginal: Cancer treatments often show early promise: tumors shrink and symptoms ease. But in many cases, the disease comes roaring back, driven by treatment-resistant cells. Part of what makes cancer so difficult to cure is that cells within a tumor are not cookie-cutter – they vary widely. Cancer cells within a tumor exist in multiple distinct malignant states, a property called “heterogeneity.” These states can also switch into one another, a property called “plasticity” — like a phone moving between airplane mode, power-saving mode, or full-performance mode. The cells share the same lineage and DNA, yet may develop into different states depending on which regulatory proteins are active in each cell, much like the normal cells in our body can have widely different states and yet carry the same DNA. Drugs used to treat a tumor are often effective only for a few of the specific states, so cells in other states remain and repopulate, making the tumor difficult to eradicate. Researchers at Biohub and collaborators from Columbia University and other institutions have developed a novel AI-based system to model how individual cells within a tumor behave and interact with drugs. The work, published in a pair of papers in Nature Genetics , supports a new hypothesis the team calls “cancer quantum biology” — that tumors of the same type have virtually identical sets of cell states across patients, and that those states interact in ways that defeat treatment. material.title: Ramaswamy’s biotech baggage haunted his political run
material.bodyOriginal: This audio is auto-generated. Please let us know if you have feedback . Vivek Ramaswamy lost Ohio’s governor’s race Tuesday amid a surge of Democratic support. It ended pretty ugly. In the final days before the midterm elections, six biotech leaders publicly urged him to withdraw a television ad featuring the estranged mother of his opponent, Amy Acton, arguing that it ignored documented childhood trauma and betrayed the evidence-based standards of their industry. The ad had already drawn criticism from both parties . Ramaswamy, who was running as a Republican, defended it. It was an unusually pointed rebuke from within the industry that had helped make Ramaswamy famous. It also raises a question that tends to get skipped when he’s characterized as a ”successful biotech entrepreneur” : Successful at what? The description isn’t invented. Roivant, the company he founded, built a network of specialized drug developers known as “Vants.” Axovant Sciences was its Alzheimer’s-focused subsidiary; other Vants went on to develop approved medicines and complete major deals. A 2023 PharmaVoice profile recalled how he had been hailed as a biotech wunderkind. But there’s a difference between raising money and creating shareholder value with producing clinical evidence that holds up. Those distinctions matter when a business record becomes a political credential. I helped tell an earlier version of that story. material.title: Accelerating the search for antimicrobial peptides with Google Antigravity
material.bodyOriginal: October 15, 2026 Science Pengfei Tian, Maxwell L. Bileschi, Zoi Tsangalidou, Sukhdeep Singh and Lucy J. Colwell New antibiotics are urgently needed to help with rising levels of antimicrobial resistance, but searching for new therapeutics is often a slow, labor-intensive process. With Google Antigravity, our agentic development platform, this process can now be made easier. Google Antigravity provides an agentic science workbench that empowers biologists to discover, structurally evaluate, and prioritize promising targets quickly, compressing what used to be a fragmented search over multiple databases into a single session. It also helps researchers scan through millions of previously uncharacterized proteins in the UniProt database using ProtNLM, a model that predicts biological function from amino acid sequences. This technical walkthrough shows how biologists used Google Antigravity to uncover a novel antimicrobial peptide candidate which has predicted activity against the pathogens involved in respiratory tract infections. The lead identified here is now undergoing wet-lab validation. Finding new antimicrobial peptides Rising antimicrobial resistance is one of the most pressing global health crises of our time and could result in an estimated 10 million annual deaths globally by 2050. To prevent this, we urgently need to discover novel therapeutics. material.title: 儿童失眠，有望迎来首款药
material.bodyOriginal: 近日，瑞士药企Idorsia宣布，其双重食欲素受体拮抗剂（DORA） 达利雷生获FDA突破性疗法认定，用于10至不满18岁儿童青少年失眠障碍。 此前，先声药业已拿下该药大中华区权益，该药也已于2025年6月在国内获批上市，用于成人失眠。 图片来源：药智数据 据悉， 美国至今没有任何获批的儿童失眠处方药 ，全球范围内现有相关药物也基本局限于褪黑素类且仅限神经发育障碍儿童使用。普通儿童的失眠治疗，始终是一扇从未被打开的门。 如今，达利雷生率先叩响了这扇门。 01 儿童失眠药市场的严峻现实 美国睡眠医学会将儿童失眠定义为：在睡眠时间安排符合年龄需求、睡眠环境适宜的情况下， 儿童仍然存在睡眠启动、睡眠持续或睡眠质量等问题，包括入睡困难、频繁夜醒、早醒、不能单独入睡等 ，并导致白天功能受损，如过度困倦、注意力不集中、学习成绩下降、情绪行为问题等。从流行病学数据看，儿童失眠并非罕见问题。据公开资料，全球儿童青少年符合临床失眠症诊断标准的患病率为9%~15%，显著高于大众认知。国内调研数据更严峻，我国6~18岁儿童青少年失眠整体患病率接近30%， 意味着每3个孩子就有1个存在不同程度的睡眠问题。 长期睡眠不足可能影响认知功能、学习效率、免疫状态和代谢健康，也与焦虑、抑郁等情绪问题存在相关性，因此， 儿童失眠具有真实临床负担，但治疗决策必须比成人更加谨慎。 《失眠症诊断和治疗指南（2025版）》明确指出，儿童青少年失眠症的发病规律、病理机制与成人存在显著差异，绝对不能直接套用成人失眠的调理和诊疗逻辑。 放眼全球，目前公开可查的儿童失眠药获批产品极其有限，且呈现出高度集中性： 成分均为褪黑素，适应症均锁死在“神经发育障碍儿童（如自闭症谱系障碍ASD、注意缺陷多动障碍ADHD）”。 具体来看，在美国， FDA至今没有批准任何专门用于治疗儿童及青少年失眠障碍的药物。 临床医生面对严重失眠的患儿，往往只能超说明书使用褪黑素、苯二氮䓬类、抗组胺药甚至部分抗精神病药，但这伴随着成瘾、认知影响和次日宿醉等巨大安全隐患。 在欧洲，缓释褪黑素微片Slenyto获批用于2–18岁自闭症谱系障碍和/或Smith-Magenis综合征儿童的失眠；在日本，Nobelpharma开发的Melatobel于2020年获批用于神经发育障碍儿童的入睡困难。在中国，2025年7月，国家药监局批准了国内首款儿童褪黑素药品——曼乐静（褪黑素颗粒），其适应症同样仅限“改善6–15岁神经发育障碍儿童的入睡困难”。 这意味着，如果一个没有神经发育障碍的10岁孩子失眠，医生依然无合规的处方药可开。庞大的需求与空白的供给之间，形成了巨大的商业与临床鸿沟。 02 DORA机制破局 达利雷生之所以被行业重视，除了适应症空白，还在于其作用机制与传统安眠药不同。 传统安眠药（如苯二氮䓬类、Z-drugs）通过广谱抑制中枢GABA系统， 强行镇静大脑，容易打乱正常睡眠结构，且具有成瘾和停药反弹风险。 而达利雷生作为双重食欲素受体拮抗剂，作用位置完全不同。食欲素是大脑中负责维持清醒的“主开关”，DORA并非将大脑“按睡”，而是选择性地阻断过度亢进的清醒驱动信号， 让自然睡眠启动，理论上更接近生理性睡眠，成瘾风险显著降低。 这一机制的临床价值，在其II期儿科研究中初露锋芒。 该项研究是全球首个、也是目前唯一一个在儿童人群中探索DORA药物的临床试验。 结果显示，在165例10-18岁失眠障碍患者中，达利雷生组（50mg）首次给药当晚，多导睡眠图测定的客观总睡眠时间较基线增加49.6分钟，较安慰剂多增约29.6分钟；入睡后觉醒时间较安慰剂减少23.1分钟。 特别值得注意的是，在合并神经发育障碍的亚组中，药物效应更强， 总睡眠时间较安慰剂多增约36.3分钟。 主要研究者Carmen M.Schröder博士指出，失眠会加重这

material.title: Translating Phase II success into Phase III readiness takes more than scale
material.bodyOriginal: Positive Phase II results clear the way for Phase III development, but a successful transition involves far more than scaling up the clinical program. Consider what can happen when a study expands into new countries. A market that looks promising based on patient availability may have a different standard of care that affects the protocol, requires additional drug sourcing, and introduces new supply and import requirements. What begins as a country-selection decision quickly becomes a clinical, regulatory, and supply decision as well. That is the less obvious challenge of moving into Phase III. The study gets larger, certainly, with more patients, sites, countries, and investigational product. But the more consequential shift is how much more interconnected the development program becomes. Country and site considerations, formulation and manufacturing requirements, supply complexity, and regulatory dependencies begin to converge. A decision in one area can create requirements or constraints in another. Phase III readiness, then, is about more than whether the clinical evidence supports moving forward. It requires understanding what needs to change across the development program, which decisions depend on one another, and what can be put in motion before Phase II is complete. Country selection has downstream consequences As Phase III expands across countries, the criteria for where to conduct the study become more complex. material.title: Sepsis is linked to 11 million deaths a year. A new machine-learning platform could help catch it within minutes
material.bodyOriginal: Ten microliters of blood flow into a disposable plastic cartridge. Inside a box with the same footprint as a laptop, it spreads into a thin layer and moves through a narrow channel. Over the next 12 minutes, a camera photographs roughly two million blood cells as they stream past. No laboratory technician waits for a blood culture. Instead, a new imaging platform, powered by a machine learning model, scans all of those cells for signs of sepsis, a life-threatening systemic response to infection that contributes to roughly 11 million deaths globally each year. Biohub scientists built that model, called Remo-ID, to run on Remoscope, an imaging cytometer the team first designed to diagnose malaria. In an early study of 47 patients and controls, Remo-ID correctly distinguished sepsis from other critical illnesses and from healthy blood in 43 cases. It did so without researchers specifying in advance which cells or cellular features to look for. The work is part of a larger bet at Biohub: that new ways of measuring biology, paired with computational models that can interpret what these technologies capture, will help scientists cure, prevent, and manage disease. Sepsis is notoriously hard to pin down. Clinicians can often recognize it from a patient’s condition and laboratory tests, but there is no single gold-standard test that can be used at the moment treatment decisions must be made. “It’s just not well quantified yet,” says Nicholas Bratvold, an engineer at Biohub who has spearheaded the sepsis project. material.title: Recordanelles capture transient gene expression in single human cells
material.bodyOriginal: Nature Biotechnology, Published online: 22 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41587-026-03350-7 RNA sequencing can capture high-resolution snapshots of a cell’s transcriptome, but transient changes in individual cells cannot be captured over long periods at a transcriptome-wide scale. Now, a synthetic organelle termed the ‘recordanelle’ can record cellular RNAs in cells for several days and be read with single-cell sensitivity.

material.title: 1400万元一针，9 例肿瘤报告！诺华「天价药」再曝安全性风险
material.bodyOriginal: 天价基因疗法 ，再曝安全性风险。 2026年11月5日，SMA Europe（欧洲脊髓性肌萎缩症协会）发布声明称：“ 自2019年首次获批以来， 诺华已收到9例既往接受Zolgensma治疗患者出现肿瘤的报告，其中2例检出载体DNA整合至患者基因组的证据。 ” 截图来源： SMA Europe Zolgensma是一款基于腺相关病毒（AAV）载体的基因治疗药物，适用于治疗6月龄及以上5q型脊髓性肌萎缩症（SMA）患者。一针定价210万美元（约合人民币1400万元），2019年首次上市时，刷新了当时的全球最高。 就是这样一款千万元天价药物，陷入了继发性肿瘤风波。据悉， 这9例肿瘤患者中， 有1例病理学提示与治疗无关、6例尚未建立因果关联。 这并非 Zolgensma首次爆出安全性风险。 2021年9月，也是该药上市的2年后，FDA召开专家咨询委员会，审查其肝毒性上。FDA文件显示当时接受 Zolgensma的500名患者中， 约有三分之一经历了肝脏相关不良事件，其中包括一例严重肝衰竭病例。 2022年8月，诺华又通报两例急性肝衰竭死亡案例，分别出现在俄罗斯和哈萨克斯坦，之后也更新了药品说明。 至于此次爆出的继发性肿瘤，Zolgensma也 在说明书的“警告与注意事项 ”早 中有所提示： 由于AAV载体DNA整合入基因组，存在理论上的致瘤风险。 截图来源：FDA 只是 截至目前，AAV整合与人类肿瘤发生之间尚缺乏明确病例证据。 既往研究显示，AAV可低频整合入宿主基因组；在新生小鼠模型中，AAV整合曾与肝细胞癌发生相关。与此同时，在犬等大动物研究中曾观察到AAV整合相关克隆扩增。 直到今年5月， 全球首例有明确分子依据的AAV整合相关人类肿瘤病例曝出。 《新英格兰医学杂志》（NEJM）刊发研究：费城儿童医院团队发现一 例重度MPS I患儿经AAV9基因治疗四年后，确诊中枢神经上皮肿瘤。 研究证实AAV载体片段 克隆整合 插入PLAG1基因，致该基因异常激活诱发肿瘤， 今年10月， NEJM又曝案例。 一名3岁男孩，婴儿型Krabbe病，接受AAVrh.10衣壳的FBX-101治疗26个月后，腰椎L2到L3出现椎旁肿块，病理确诊为GLI1基因改 变相关肿瘤。 当时，有学者认为， 仅凭两例肿瘤断定AAV基因治疗普遍致癌，为时过早。 分子机制无可辩驳，但人群因果并未坐实。 这两名患儿都有共同的高危背景，年龄极小、做过造血干细胞移植、接受过清髓性化疗或免疫抑制。 这些治疗本身就会带来DNA损伤并削弱免疫系统，很难把肿瘤完全归因于AAV。 并 且分母 依然很小，且 Zolgensma 因果关系尚未建立。 那么，这么一款有肝毒性风险、继发性肿瘤可能的疗法，定价还要 1400万元，合理吗？ 截图来源：电影《我不是药神》 回答这个问题之前，需要先 引入一个经济学概念： QALY，质量调整生命年。一个QALY代表一年完美健康的生命。 （所以，某种意义而言，生命是可以被定价的） 上世纪八十年代，美国卫生经济学家以肾透析治疗的成本效益分析，每QALY 5万美元。 2010年代，美国临床和经济评价研究所（ICER） 开始使用 10万到15万美元每QALY 作为新的基准区间。 套到Zolgensma上：没有治疗，SMA 1型患儿中位生存期约两年，生活质量极低。若这一针能让患儿正常成长、活到平均预期寿命（假设70岁）并维持较高生活质量（QALY系数0.8），可创造约54个QALY（68年×0.8）； 212.5万美元除以54，每QALY约3.9万美元。 这样算的话，Zolgensma不但不贵，似乎还很“便宜”。 诺华也在用 类似的逻辑为其定价辩护： 在Zolgensma之前，SMA的主要治疗选择是Biogen的Spinraza（诺西那生钠）。 诺西那生钠第一年的费用是75万

material.title: FDA Approves First Plasmid DNA-based Immunotherapy for Adults with Recurrent Respiratory Papillomatosis
material.bodyOriginal: FDA News Release Groundbreaking therapy provides additional treatment option that fights the disease at its source, not only its symptoms For Immediate Release: October 30, 2026 The U.S. Food and Drug Administration today granted accelerated approval for Voceryq (doruxapapogene ralaplasmid and lalikinogene sifuplasmid-gxfd) for treatment of adults with recurrent respiratory papillomatosis (RRP), a rare disease caused by human papillomavirus (HPV) that leads to the formation of small, wart-like growths in the patient’s airways. This approval, the first for a plasmid DNA-based immunotherapy in the U.S., offers patients a new therapeutic option that targets the root cause of RRP and has been shown to reduce the burden of surgical intervention, representing an important step forward for a patient population with limited treatment options. “Adults living with recurrent respiratory papillomatosis often face an exhausting and relentless cycle of repeated surgeries, managing their disease, but never truly escaping it. Today’s approval represents a meaningful scientific breakthrough: a plasmid DNA-based immunotherapy that harnesses the body’s own immune system to fight the underlying cause of RRP,” said Karim Mikhail, B. Pharm., M.S., Director of the Center for Biologics Evaluation and Research (CBER) . “For patients, that could mean fewer surgeries, fewer disruptions, and more time living their lives on their own terms. material.title: Graeme Clark, Erwin Hochmair, Ingeborg Hochmair, Michael Merzenich, and Blake Wilson receive the 2026 Merkin Prize at the Broad Institute for the modern cochlear implant
material.bodyOriginal: Broad Institute's gene-editing technologies—CRISPR-Cas9, base editing, and prime editing—are being tested in more than 25 clinical trials to treat or cure leukemias, rare genetic diseases, high cholesterol, and other conditions. NIH-funded discoveries from the Broad Institute are powering nearly 20 clinical trials from companies testing new treatments for diseases like cancer and heart disease. Broad Institute developed a technology — partly supported by NIH funding — that can detect trace amounts of cancer DNA from blood tests and help cancer patients find out their risk of disease recurrence earlier. Using NIH funding, the Broad’s Rare Genomes Project has worked with more than 1,300 families from all 50 U.S. states to diagnose rare genetic diseases. Broad Clinical Labs has directly partnered with tens of thousands of cancer patients to analyze their DNA and accelerate research. During the COVID-19 pandemic, Broad Institute launched a large-scale diagnostic testing lab that processed over 37 million tests and saved state and federal programs nearly $2 billion. The Broad Institute's Cancer Dependency Map helps cancer researchers and drug developers discover therapeutic targets for new cancer treatments. gnomAD, a large human genetic variant reference database developed by the Broad Institute with NIH funding, has contributed to over 13 million genetic disease diagnoses since its launch in 2014. material.bodyOriginal: “ 要前瞻布局建设重大科技基础设施，强化高端科研仪器、科学数据、科技期刊等基础条件自主保障， 推进人工智能赋能科学研究 ——习近平总书记2026年7月8日在两院院士大会、中国科协十一大上的讲话 ” “以人工智能引领科研范式变革”， 已经从行业 共识 上升为国家任务。 2026年10 月印发的《中共中央国务院关于发展新质生产力的意见》，将“全面实施‘人工智能+’行动”列为推动科技创新与产业创新深度融合的重大任务；“十五五”规划纲要明确要 “ 抢占人工智能产业应用制高点，全方位赋能千行百业 ”。 在此背景下， 由上海人工智能研究院、上海交通大学主动健康战略与发展研究院、 生物谷 主办，华东师范大学丽娃皮肤健康研究院、加州医学创新研究院 CalMI2、梅斯医学联合主办 的 2026亚太科研与工程智能大会(2026 Asia-Pacific AI for Science Conference) ，定于2026年12月12-13日在上海举科学会堂举行。 联合主办介绍 本次大会的联合主办单位之一— 华东师范大学丽娃皮肤健康研究院 ，是华东师范大学面向"健康中国"战略、聚焦皮肤健康交叉学科建设设立的新型研究机构，由徐林担任院长、杨浩然担任副院长。 研究院以医工交叉为特色，长期联合知名三甲医院 皮肤科 及相关健康科技企业，围绕城市环境与人类行为对居民健康的影响开展系统性研究，推动皮肤健康 管理 向" 精准 化、定制化、普惠化"升级。 研究院为本次大会 "AI驱动生命健康的转化前沿" 议题提供了最鲜活的实践注脚——丽娃研究院将持续为大会贡献"丽娃智慧"，让AI for Science真正走向民生与产业一线。 0 1 专家介绍 华东师范大学丽娃皮肤健康研究院 副院长杨浩然 教授受邀要出席本次会议并发表主题报告。 杨浩然，华东师范大学地理科学学院教授、博导，现任华东师范大学丽娃皮肤健康研究院副院长、中国生物工程学会数字化医工技术专委会副主任委员、中国抗 衰老 促进会皮肤慢病与健康管理分会人工智能应用委员会副组长，中国自然资源学会国土空间规划研究专业委员会委员。 科研成果 主要研究方向为城市环境与人类行为对居民健康影响，长期联合知名三甲医院皮肤科以及相关健康科技公司开展城市环境行为与皮肤慢病关联研究，开发了环境与行为AI慢病管理系统，并申请国家专利2项及软著4项。近五年发表学术论文40余篇（含Cell子刊、Nature系列刊物2篇），主持国家及省部级项目6项，相关成果形成决策咨询获中央主要领导及省部级领导批示，并担任《地理科学》青年编委及《皮肤科学通报》特邀编委。 大会信息 会议名称 2026亚太科研与工程智能大会 2026 Asia-Pacific AI for Science Conference 会议时间 2026年12月12-13日 会议地点 上海科学会堂 会议主题 智启科研全新范式・共筑亚太创新生态 指导单位 上海交通大学 主办单位 上海人工智能研究院、上海交通大学主动健康战略与发展研究院、生物谷 联合主办 华东师范大学丽娃皮肤健康研究院、 加州医学创新研究院 CalMI2、 梅斯医学 支持单位 上海科技发展 基金 会、上海科学会堂服务中心 01 SPECIAL GUESTS 特邀嘉宾阵容 乐玉成 外交部 原副部长 第十九届中央候补委员 国家广播电视总局原副局长 曾任国家广播电视总局党组成员 贾伟平 中国工程院 院士 发展中国家科学院（TWAS）院士 中国医学科学院学部委员 973首席科学家 上海交通大学讲席教授 上海交通大学医学院附属第六人民医院主任医师 博士生导师 李景虹 中国科学院 院士 分析化学家 清华大学化学系教授、 博士生导师 学术委员会主任 分析中心主任 分析化学所所长 宋海涛 英国工程技术学会 会士 联合国人工智能问题独立国际科学小组成员

material.title: A push for speedier drug approvals doesn’t promise smooth market sailing
material.bodyOriginal: This audio is auto-generated. Please let us know if you have feedback . The FDA recently ramped up its efforts to streamline drug development and review when it launched the Rare Disease Framework Initiative . The initiative is part of an ongoing push that includes other ways to shorten regulatory timelines, such as the Commissioner's National Priority Voucher program and the Expedited Investigational New Drug Pilot Program . But efforts to shave time off the approval process don’t guarantee smooth sailing for drug developers when working with regulators, according to Sahir Raoof , founder and managing partner of the early-stage fund Proximal Ventures . This is especially true after nearly two years of upheaval at the FDA. While biotech execs can’t predict or control what’s going on inside the agency, they can de-risk their regulatory journey by communicating earlier and more frequently than they might think is necessary. Being in constant contact can also help biotech companies learn about and adapt to FDA staff turnover more quickly. “In a potentially changing landscape, I think the most powerful tool is having a high-touch engagement model with the agency,” Raoof said. material.title: Vir hepatitis D drug succeeds in first pivotal study
material.bodyOriginal: An article from A program that’s survived Vir’s pivot away from infectious disease research hit all of its study objectives and appeared more potent than a rival drug also in late-stage development. Published Nov. 9, 2026 Vir Biotechnology is developing a drug combination for chronic hepatitis D infections. Getty Images An experimental two-drug combination from Vir Biotechnology has succeeded in the first of three Phase 3 trials against chronic hepatitis D, the company said Sunday. Vir’s drugs, “elebsiran” and “tobevibart,” met their main objective in the study by largely eliminating detectable signs of the virus and normalizing levels of an important liver enzyme in 44% of treatment participants after 48 weeks. By comparison, none in a “delayed treatment” cohort achieved those results, according to Vir. The regimen also met a key secondary endpoint focused solely on dropping viral levels, with 79% of treated patients achieving a treatment response. Two additional Phase 3 trials are ongoing and should produce data early next year. Results from all three studies, if positive, would support a regulatory submission in 2027. Vir was initially formed to go after infectious diseases and, in 2021, successfully brought to market a COVID-19 antibody drug called Xevudy. But the company has since restructured and changed course. It’s now primarily working on T-cell engagers for cancer. Vir clung to some of its infectious disease research, however.
